samples.summary: Undo jump target is only cleared when it is applied, so a target whose tab never mounts a SheetView survives and lands late
samples.evidence: The new `onUndoJumpHandled` fires only on the success path of the effect (`sheet-view.tsx:1465-1471`): the effect returns early when `undoJumpTarget.selection.tabId !== tabId` or when `sheetRef.current` is undefined. Two reachable cases leave the host's target set indefinitely: (a) the undo landed in a tab the host renders as something other than SheetView — `DataSourceView` / `LakehouseView` in `document-detail.tsx:753-766`, `SharedLakehouseUnavailable` in `shared-document.tsx:322-326` — so no mount can ever report it handled; (b) the user switches to another tab before the target tab's engine finishes its async `initialize()` (mount effect at sheet-view.tsx:1050-1067 resolves asynchronously), after which the effect's tabId guard blocks it. In case (b) the stale target is not dropped, and the moment the user later returns to that tab a fresh mount (lastHandledUndoJumpRequestIdRef reset to 0) applies `focusUndoSelection` — moving the selection for an undo that happened arbitrarily long ago, which is exactly the class of bug this callback was added to remove.

samples.summary: handleUndoJump sets activeTabId to an unvalidated tab id; a tab removed by a peer mounts YorkieStore on a missing worksheet
samples.evidence: `handleUndoJump` (shared-document.tsx:221-225) does `setActiveTabId(selection.tabId)` with no check that `root.tabs[selection.tabId]` still exists. `selection.tabId` comes from operation paths of a replayed *local* history step, which can name a tab a remote peer has since deleted. On the resulting render `activeTab` is undefined, so the ternary at shared-document.tsx:322-334 falls through to `<SheetView tabId={activeTabId} …>`; SheetView's mount effect immediately builds `new YorkieStore(doc, tabId, readOnly)` (sheet-view.tsx:1050) and `initialize()` reads the grid via `YorkieStore.getSheet()` (yorkie-store.ts:133-135) which returns `undefined`, and `getWorksheetKeys`/`getWorksheetEntries` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-grid.ts:170) dereferences `ws.cells` → TypeError inside the promise. `initialize(...).then(...)` has no `.catch`, so this is an unhandled rejection and a blank grid until the corrective effect at shared-document.tsx:280-289 resets activeTabId to tabs[0]. The same unvalidated jump exists in document-detail.tsx:160, which has no such corrective effect at all (its effect at line 335-341 only fires when activeTabId is null), so there the bad tab id sticks.

samples.summary: readOnly now short-circuits undo()/redo() but canUndo()/canRedo() still report the raw Yorkie history
samples.evidence: `undo()`/`redo()` gained `if (this.readOnly) return { success: false };` (yorkie-store.ts:1285, 1291) but `canUndo()`/`canRedo()` (1370-1376) still return `this.doc.history.canUndo()/canRedo()` unconditionally. Any consumer that asks the store whether undo is available on a read-only mount gets `true` for an operation the store will now refuse — the sibling read-only/memory stores keep the two consistent (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:327-341 return false from all four). No production UI reads it today (only the dev hunt bridge, sheet.canUndo), so impact is confined to a misleading capability report.

finding.summary: Stale `undoJumpTarget` is re-applied after any SheetView remount other than a history restore
finding.evidence: `undoJumpTarget` is only ever cleared in `handleHistoryRestored` (document-detail.tsx:182). `SheetView` remembers the handled request in a mount-local ref (`lastHandledUndoJumpRequestIdRef`, sheet-view.tsx:244), which resets to 0 on any unmount/remount — and `historyResetToken` is not the only remount: `SheetView` is unmounted whenever the active tab is a datasource (document-detail.tsx:746) or lakehouse (751) tab, and whenever `!ready || !activeTabId` swaps in the `Loader` (744). Sequence: a cross-tab undo jumps to Sheet2 and is handled; the user clicks a datasource tab (SheetView unmounts) and then returns to Sheet2; the effect at sheet-view.tsx:1443 sees a non-null `undoJumpTarget` whose `requestId` (>0) no longer matches the fresh ref (0), so it calls `focusUndoSelection` again and hijacks/scrolls the user's selection to a long-past undo. The in-code justification ("`historyResetToken` remounts `SheetView`") assumes that is the only remount, which the datasource/lakehouse/Loader branches contradict.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim — that `undoJumpTarget` is cleared only in `handleHistoryRestored` — is false in this tree. `document-detail.tsx:171-173` defines `handleUndoJumpHandled` (`setUndoJumpTarget(null)`), passed to the view at `document-detail.tsx:775` as `onUndoJumpHandled`, and `sheet-view.tsx:1465-1471` invokes `onUndoJumpHandledRef.current?.()` in the same effect body immediately after `sheet.focusUndoSelection(...)`. The host therefore drops the target the moment the grid applies it, so by the time the datasource (`document-detail.tsx:757`), lakehouse (`762`) or Loader (`755-756`) branch unmounts `SheetView` and a remount zeroes `lastHandledUndoJumpRequestIdRef` (`sheet-view.tsx:254`), `undoJumpTarget` is null and the effect short-circuits at `sheet-view.tsx:1456`. The finding also mischaracterizes the in-code justification: the comments at `document-detail.tsx:164-170`, `188-193` and `sheet-view.tsx:171-177`, `1467-1470` explicitly enumerate the datasource/lakehouse/loader remounts as the reason the handled-callback exists, rather than assuming `historyResetToken` is the only remount. Only the null-engine pending case (`sheet-view.tsx:1462-1463`) leaves a target standing, which is the intended deferred-apply path, not a stale re-application.

finding.summary: The shared sheet view passes no `onUndoJump`, so cross-tab undo is invisible for editor-role share links — and the prop's stated justification is false
finding.evidence: sheet-view.tsx's `onUndoJump` doc-comment claims it may be "omitted (the read-only share view) ... which is moot there since undo is disabled". But `shared-document.tsx:198` computes `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, so an `editor`-role share link renders `<SheetView tabId={activeTabId} readOnly={false} peerJumpTarget={...} />` (line 300) with undo fully enabled and no `onUndoJump`. In that surface an undo whose step belongs to another tab mutates the CRDT and neither switches tabs nor moves the selection — exactly the "undo looks like it did nothing" defect this change exists to fix, left in place on one of two sheet surfaces, with an inline comment asserting it cannot happen.

verdict.reason: The finding claims shared-document.tsx's SheetView passes no `onUndoJump`, leaving cross-tab undo broken for editor-role share links. The file's sole SheetView render site does pass it. packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:327-334 renders `<SheetView tabId={activeTabId} readOnly={readOnly} peerJumpTarget={peerJumpTarget} undoJumpTarget={undoJumpTarget} onUndoJump={handleUndoJump} onUndoJumpHandled={handleUndoJumpHandled} />`. The supporting machinery is present too: `undoJumpTarget` state and `undoJumpSeq` ref at L208-212, `handleUndoJump` at L221-225 (bumps the sequence, calls `setActiveTabId(selection.tabId)`, sets the target) with a doc-comment that explicitly handles the editor-role case ("An `editor`-role share link mounts the grid writable, so Cmd+Z runs here too ... Follow it the same way `DocumentLayout` does"), and `handleUndoJumpHandled` at L227-229. Grep confirms line 327 is the only SheetView usage in the file (import at L15). The secondary claim about a false justification is also wrong: sheet-view.tsx:163-170 reads "Every host that mounts this view writable passes it — a `viewer` share link is the one mount where it can be omitted, since undo is refused there by both the engine's `readOnly` and `YorkieStore.undo`", which correctly scopes the omission to viewer mounts and matches the code. The finding's cited line numbers (198, 300) do not match the working tree (204, 327), indicating the evidence came from a different revision.
